name: SCD30 CO2 sensor module
description: Sensirion NDIR CO2 sensor module (0-40000 ppm output, ±(30 ppm + 3 %) from 400-10000 ppm) with on-board temperature and relative humidity sensing, I2C interface (results as 32-bit floats), new reading every 2 s by default. Runs on 3.3-5.5 V; SDA/SCL have 45 k pull-ups to 3 V inside the module. Sold as: Sensirion SCD30 sensor module (article 1-101625-10, also sold by SparkFun as SEN-15112; 7-pin 2.54 mm row VDD, GND, TX/SCL, RX/SDA, RDY, PWM, SEL), I2C address 0x61 (fixed).
eli5: Measures how much carbon dioxide is in the room (plus temperature and humidity), so you can tell when it is time to open a window.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: Printed TX/SCL on the module. I2C clock (internal 45 k pull-up to 3 V; do not pull above 3.0 V)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: Printed RX/SDA on the module. I2C data (internal 45 k pull-up to 3 V; do not pull above 3.0 V)

pins.name: RDY
pins.description: Data-ready output, high when a new reading is waiting (optional)

pins.name: PWM
pins.description: PWM output of the CO2 reading, 0-5000 ppm (not used with I2C)

pins.name: SEL
pins.description: Interface select: leave floating or tie to GND for I2C (high = Modbus UART)

buildNotes: The SCD30 is slow on I2C: run the bus at 50 kHz or less (freq=50000) and let the sensor stretch the clock (up to 30 ms, 150 ms about once a day). It does not support repeated start, so write the command and read in two separate transfers.

Start continuous measurement with 0x0010 + pressure word + CRC (0x00 0x10 0x00 0x00 0x81 = no pressure compensation). It keeps measuring after power cycles; new reading every 2 s by default (0x4600 sets 2-1800 s).

Poll get_data_ready_status 0x0202 (wait >3 ms, read 3 bytes; word = 1 when ready), then read_measurement 0x0300 (wait >3 ms, read 18 bytes): CO2, temperature, humidity as big-endian IEEE-754 floats, a CRC after every 16-bit half.
CRC-8 poly 0x31, init 0xFF (CRC(0xBEEF) = 0x92). Commands with an argument need the CRC of the argument too.
SDA/SCL have 45 k pull-ups to 3 V inside the module and the inputs only tolerate 3.0 V: with a 5 V supply, never pull the I2C lines up to 5 V (use a level shifter on a 5 V board).
Leave SEL floating (or on GND) for I2C. Draws about 19 mA on average, peaks of 75 mA while measuring.
The sensor needs up to 2 s after power-up before it answers. Do not touch the optical cavity; keep it away from the regulator and microcontroller, which warm the air.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from scd30 import SCD30

# The SCD30 wants a slow bus (50 kHz) and stretches the clock.
i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=50000)
sensor = SCD30(i2c)
while True:
    co2, t, h = sensor.read()  # waits for the next 2-second reading
    print('CO2=%dppm T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (co2, t, h))
    time.sleep(2)
